newsitem.title: USA: Corning posts big jump in second-quarter profits.
newsitem.headline: Corning posts big jump in second-quarter profits.

text.p: Corning Inc. said Tuesday that its profits jumped in the second quarter, helped by strong growth in consumer housewares and communications technology products such as optical fibers.
The company said its net income for the three months ended June 30 soared to $127.0 million, or 56 cents a share, from $37.0 million, or 16 cents a share, a year earlier
The 1996 results included a loss of $56.8 million, or 25 cents a share, from discontinued operations. Otherwise, net income would have been $93.8 million, or 41 cents a share, for that quarter.
Excluding the loss, net income from continuing operations rose by 35 percent, Corning said.

"We are pleased with the results for the quarter," Chairman Roger G. Ackerman said in a statement. "Our investments in optical fiber, cable and photonic technologies are clearly yielding significant returns."
Corning announced earlier this year that it is exploring the divestiture of its consumer housewares business.
Ackerman said the company's outlook for the year remained strong, with demand for communications-related products continuing to increase worldwide.

Corning, which is based in Corning, N.Y., manufactures optical fiber, cable and components, high performance glass and components for televisions, and other electronic displays for communications and communications-related industries.
It also produces advanced materials for the scientific and environmental markets as well as consumer products, such as the company's famous glass cookware.
Corning's stock added 44 cents to $56.44 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
